items.title: PengLang, indepth
items.text:
PengLang Type DSL Designed by bebeday10 Developer bebeday10 First appeared May 31 2026 Stable release 0.0.1 OS Cross-platform License MIT License Influenced by Python Influenced FishLang

PengLang is a domain-specific language that let's penguins code in Style™.

bebeday10 began working on PengLang on May 31st 2026.

PengLang has gained extensive use in the fish community. It is widely taught to penguins1. PengLang has consistently ranked top penguin on the Penguin Community Index.

items.title: History
items.text: PengLang was conceived on May 31st 2026 with the idea of "What if Python was penguins?"2.

items.title: Variables
items.text:
Penguins think. They think a lot. Like... a lot a lot. Like too much. Well, the penguins need memory.

Note

Do not fear the "memory". It will not eat the RAM. Like a bit. But it is like a bit. Do not fear.

We have made the memory thing. Make sure you remember.

variables.py
import penglang.penglang as pl # (1)!

pl.penguin_variable("banana", 2) # (2)!
better_banana = 2 # (3)!

pl.say(pl.banana) # (4)!
pl.say(better_banana) # (5)!
  1. use this way if you want runtime variables.
  2. the authentic, PengLang way of making variables. Very janky.
  3. the pythonic way of making variables. not full PengLang, but recognized if you want a less janky way of coding.
  4. use the module name when using the authentic way.
  5. use no module name when using the pythonic way.

items.title: Features
items.text:
There lives many features. Too many features.

Can we cut down the features?

No. Not exactly.

items.title: OOBE
items.text:
PengLang has a OOBE (Out-Of-Box Experience). It gets installed when you install PengLang.

Sorry, what?

An OOBE is normally an initial setup process. In PengLang, it is used to "setup the penguins".

items.title: Naming scheme
items.text:
Scheme? Pyramid...

No.

The naming scheme of the OOBE (ooh-beh) is "Penguin Box Of Stuff" (peng-hu-ween boh-ks ove sht-uhffe) or the PBOS (pee-boast).

items.title: Startup
items.text: It starts when one makes a PBOS. Things like "Language/Region", "Let's connect you to the PengNet", "Set up your Penguin account" appear.

items.title: Get out!
items.text:
When one calls, "Get something!" or the PBOS itself, it randomly chooses one of the things in it and takes it out of the PBOS. They can also choose more than one at the same time. If you get chosen, get ready to experience the OOBE.

What happens:

  • It gets out of the box
  • You are no longer part of the box
  • You are not counted in the length of the box
  • The box no longer has you
  • If you are the only one, and you got pulled, the box is now wrong.

items.title: What to do
items.text: Live life outside the box. Be free.

items.title: What happens to the OOBE
items.text: It has you removed. After that, if there are no more, the PBOS will shout at the maker when they try to take another thing.

items.title: A clarification on everything in the Features section
items.text:
Penguins do not spread misinformation here. Everything here is real and factual1.

The reasons why penguins do this is to make visitors... less confused. Otherwise, you'd be wondering why you'd get an AttributeError on a clearly stated page on the documentation.

  1. Unless stated otherwise. Penguins are truthful. Very. ↩

items.title: Fish
items.text:
Fish are foods for penguins to eat. They are also living water creatures under the sea.

In PengLang, fish can swim both ways after innovation by Pengnology™1.

Fish can swim at a record-breaking 30 swim ticks per second.

Fun fact

Fish favor the right way.

What happened to the left?

Whenever they went left, they encountered a wall.

  1. Swimming is cool. ↩

items.text:
The horse, is a decorator in the main module of PengLang.

It may seem very out of place. But, penguins need to use these horses.

What is the horse doing?

The horse neighs. Very much. It neighs. Neighs. 1. Says "neeeeeigh! 🐎🐎🐎 hoooorse!" 2. Starts the command. 3. Says "the horse has finished its thing!"

items.title: Mathematical machine
items.text:
Some penguins hated doing math.

So they made something to do it for them.

Are they lazy? What's wrong with them?

True. How would they know?

items.title: How does one math?
items.text:
Simply, 

import penglang.modules.pengmath.pengmathmachine as pm
import penglang as pl
machine = pm.PenguinMathMachine()
long_depression = "1+2" # (1)!
pl.say(machine.evaluate_math(long_depression, step_show=True, main_step_show_only=False)) # (2)!

  1. This is the long depression because many non-mathematicians don't know the answer to this expression.
  2. The machine has decided to help them solve this seemingly impossible question.

It will then do math.

1: ['1', '2'] (doing + (add)) # (1)!
2: [1.0, 2.0] (doing + (add)) (evaluates as 3.0) # (2)!
3.0
  1. The machine will talk in a language no one understands.
  2. The penguins are questioning how it did the impossible question.

Clearly so, it has done the question.

That's extremely hard. You're sure that's the correct answer?

We're not sure. The math machine is.

items.title: What can it do?
items.text:
It can do many.

  • Add (+)
  • Subtract (-)
  • Multiply (*)
  • Divide (/)
  • Floor divide (//)
  • Exponentiation (** or ^)
  • Factorial (!)
Pro tip

The factorial is customized. Doing a double factorial (!!), is !2. !n = ! of n amount.

What?

You'll figure it out.

  • Termial
A termial is...

A termial is triangle. Example: 3? = 3+2+1

  • Remainder (%)
  • Root (r)
Ultra Pro tip

nth root: _rn

items.title: Translating
items.text:
Penguins and dogs cannot converse with each other. They want to converse with each other.

That's why they made a penguin translate machine.

Why do dogs want to talk. Aren't they weird?

You have never heard of unity in your entire life.

How are you going to work together with your friends1?

items.title: Basics
items.text:
The penguin translate machine has a translate_from, and a translate_to. Translate from is the one that came first, and translate to is the one you want.

Penguin

I thought I fell, Ante is so high, One stopping burger,

A burger?

It's a sandwich.

A sandwich?

It's 2 bread top and bottom with things in the middle.

Bread?

Good penguin food.

The above may be controversial, but who cares?

Lie all night. Ooowouh, ooowouh! When, I translate from, I get the language it was. If a dog speaks dog,

A dog speaks dog?

It's common knowledge. Did you get sweesh swashed?

Dog is that language, If it gets translated, Into a penguin-understandable thing, It is translated to.

To what?

To your brain.

I'm not that smart in maths2. What did you say?

I said it went to your brain.

Intense jazz plays

For example, If you have a dog that says "woof woof", and you have a penguin that says "buaak buaak", you may be interested in this. 

import penglang as pl
import penglang.modules.pengtranslate as pt

pl.say(
    pt.PenguinTranslateMachine(
        translate_from="woof woof",
        translate_to="buaak buaak",
    ).translate("woof. i am dog. woof.")

)
Penguins might get: 
buua.aiaamadug.abuua.
Penguins will understand what it means.

items.title: With inverse and back
items.text:
Penguins can make letters mapped to their counterparts. For example:

import penglang as pl
import penglang.modules.pengtranslate as pt

text = pt.PenguinTranslateMachine(
    ps.alphabet[::-1],

).translate(
    "hello world"
)

pl.say(text)

will say: 

svool dliow

This is because A -> Z, B -> Y, and so on.

What does it mean?

For example, The first letter of the alphabet is A, and the last is Y. The second letter of the alphabet is B, and the second last is V.

Wait...

I have waited long and there has been nothing.

A rhetorical question is a question that doesn't want an answer.

items.title: Making units
items.text:
Automatically, your translate_to is by letter. If you want to stitch up your letters, that's called a word according to penguins.

translate_to can be: ["banana", "horse", "penguin"] and it will replace the whole word.

items.title: When making a new translating machine
items.text:
1. At PengTranslate, a penguin goes to the Translate Factory™.
  2. They take your translate_to and translate_from.
  3. They do important checks.
    1. Check if your translate_to is anything.
      1. If not:
      2. Go to PengSymbol
      3. Get alphanumerics.
    2. Check if your translate_to is a number.
      1. If so:
      2. String it.
    3. Check if your translate_to is a string.
      1. If so:
      2. List it.
    4. Check if your translate_from is anything.
      1. If not:
      2. Go to PengSymbol
      3. Get alphanumerics.
    5. Check everything else.
    6. Stich everything up with PengIterable's list_combine into translate_key.

items.title: When translating a text
items.text:
1. Take the text, and turn it into a list.
  2. Make a loop for each letter in the text.
    1. Make that letter into translate_key's letter corresponding to that key's letter.
    2. If the letter corresponding to that key is not found: continue.
  3. Return the text joined.

  1. If you have any. ↩

  2. It's not maths. ↩

items.title: Bananas
items.text: PengLang has a thing known as bananas. They are nutritious for the average penguin1. Penguins eat them because they are "cool".

items.title: What They Have
items.text:
• name: Clearly, penguins need to check their banana names.

    I'm in a predicament. Why do they have names?

    Because bananas are very important to name. Or else, how would you call your banana? If they said "Banana!", who knows what will happen.

  • size: Used to check the BMI.

  • weight: Stronger the better! Mainly for fighting other bananas.

    Note

    They are also used to prevent sweesh swashing.

  • freshness: Make sure they aren't rotten.

  • potassium: What's the point of eating a banana if there isn't any potassium?

  • species: The type of banana.

    Note

    These are very different from names. Beware!

    A quote from a penguin

    Oh me oh, I fo a lo, My names got mixed up, Ended up a trial of bananas, Help!

  • peeled, eaten: Status of the banana

items.title: What They Can Do
items.text:
• peel: Peel the banana.
  • eat: Eat the banana.
  • throw: Throw the banana.
Sequences

To eat the banana, you must peel the banana. To throw the banana, you must eat the banana2.

  • get potassium: Check how potassiumized the banana is.
  • bmi: Get the BMI. Formula: weight ÷ size²

  • get weight category: Some penguins go on a diet. Lighter the more diet-friendly!

    • 0-1: tiny banana
    • 1-3: normal banana
    • 3-5: big banana
    • >5: chonky banana

  • quality ratio: How rich the banana is. Used to check the best bananas.

  • Formula: (Potassium * Freshness) / (BMI * 50)

  1. They are a hazard if they aren't average.

    I have fed them a banana, what do I do?

    You can't do anything but watch them. We hope we could bring better news.

    ↩

  2. A penguin once tried throwing before eating. It ended up that the banana flew and caused a massive earthquake. Didn't go so well. ↩

items.text:

Quote

Hey everyone! Say heeey, Say hoooe! Meet the person of the karaoke! Jazz music plays in the background Every time I don't drop CDs, I always make sure to play them... items.text:
One time in a faraway crowd, a penguin dances. They proceeded to go on a roundabout. They went left with no pain2.

But then, a different penguin went right, And a painful tsunami came by.

Everyone sweeshed and swashed.

Even the ones that went left in the whole tsunami.

When and why were there tsunamis in such a peaceful island?

When the penguin went right.3

<Insert tsunami here>

The world shakes...

items.text:
Racing penguins are racers that race on a racetrack1. The reasons they race are because they want to give back to the family. They also climb trees to increase endurance3.

How does one give back?

Using the power of penguins.

items.title: Motivations
items.text: Racing penguins walk into a tree sometimes. This is known as "Motivation". Motivation is very important for the penguins to race faster and further.

They use willpower to fight. Racing penguins thought that sounded great, and they followed the same way.

items.title: Not sure how much quality<sup>3</sup> to get?
items.text:
When it comes to PengLang quality3, some people need more1 quality and some people need less. If you’re unsure how much you’ll need, finding out how much you’re currently using can help you choose.

On your PengLang, go to Settings > General > PengLang Quality to learn how much quality you’re using, how you’re using it and how much you have left. On other languages1, go to Settings > Device > Quality.

If you’re nearing your quality limit with a lot of PengLang files3, PengKaraoke or PengImage rendering7, it’s a good1 idea to consider a better quality model6.

If you’re not using a lot of quality and rarely use PengLang or don’t take many PengImage renders7, a PengLang with a worse quality3 may2 be better for you.

items.title: The current tip
items.text:
Tip #3: For the new v0.10.0: Use bananas

Bananas are a great way to increase banana healthiness. Penguins can make bananas by importing it. 

import penglang.modules.pengbanana

thing = PenguinBanana()
They then can use these bananas to eat. Don't eat rotten bananas!

Only works on 0.10.0 and above!

This feature only works on 0.10.0 and above. Beware the penguins of 0.9.0 and below.

items.title: Archive 1
items.text:
Tip #2: Awesome tip for Windows users

If you press and hold the undo/redo button on your mouse on the Start button and release it outside of the Start button, it will be stuck in its hover state until you interact with it again.

Tip #1: Dancing

Has your penguin ever felt like... dancing? Use dance, which is in the main PengLang module. Penguins can dance whatever style they want. They can scream too.

Note

Dancing is in magenta!
